user_consequence: A player or coach sees one number on the Team/Operations rail item, the mobile bottom-nav 5th column, and the More sheet row for it, with no way to tell from the number whether it means an unread announcement, a pending task, or an unseen travel itinerary -- three different objects with three different clearing actions on three different screens. Opening the destination the badge points at does not necessarily clear the count the user saw, because the number was never about that one destination.
mechanism: summarizeMoreTab (more-nav.ts) sums badge across every hidden overflow item with no per-category breakdown. Upstream, buildPlayerRailSections composes the player's single 'Team' rail item's badge as announcements+tasks+travel summed (nav-registry.ts:433), and MoreNavSheet's OverflowRow renders only the one combined integer (no sub-breakdown) next to the row label.
expected: Each rendered count has one exact, documented set definition and one clearing action; a combined destination (like Team) either shows a per-category breakdown or the badge is scoped to a single well-defined event type.
actual: badges.announcements + badges.tasks + badges.travel are summed into one opaque integer with no UI decomposition; the More sheet's aggregate is a second, further-summed total across every hidden nav item.
proposed_fix: Either (a) give the Team rail item a documented composite-count contract (a small typed structure the row itself decomposes on render, e.g. an icon-and-count per sub-category) or (b) split the Team badge into the individual sub-destination badges the way Calendar and Messages already are, and update more-nav.ts's summarizeMoreTab to preserve category identity instead of a bare sum.

user_consequence: A coach's 'Operations' rail/bottom-nav item is wired to show a badge for pending Tasks, but that badge can never light up for a coach no matter how many tasks are outstanding on the team -- it silently always reads 'no badge', which a coach will reasonably interpret as 'no attention needed' when the wiring simply never populates it.
mechanism: notification-badge-context.tsx's coach branch unconditionally sets tasks to 0 on every successful poll (there is no coach-facing 'pending tasks' concept in CoachNotificationCounts at all -- see coach-notifications.ts, which returns only calendarNotifications and unreadMessages). nav-registry.ts still wires badges.tasks into the coach Operations rail item's badge as if it were a live count.
expected: A badge wired into the nav registry corresponds to a count that can actually become nonzero for that role, or the registry omits the badge for a role it doesn't apply to.
actual: badges.tasks is force-set to 0 for every coach poll; the coach Operations badge is permanently dead.
proposed_fix: Either give coaches a real signal here (e.g. count of assignments approaching/overdue across the roster, if that is a wanted feature) or drop the badge wiring for the coach Operations item entirely so the UI does not imply a live count that can never appear. Needs a product decision on which.

user_consequence: A transient read failure on the unified notifications-unread count or the CoachHelm alert count makes the bell badge and the CoachHelm rail badge drop to a confident zero, indistinguishable from 'nothing to see' -- exactly the failure mode the file's own comments say the messages/announcements/tasks counts were fixed to avoid.
mechanism: notification-badge-context.tsx holds the PREVIOUS value for announcements/tasks/messages/travel/calendarNotifications on a failed poll (guarded by `if (result.success && result.data)`), but notificationsUnread and coachhelm are unconditionally reset to 0 both on `success:false` and inside their own catch blocks -- the 'hold previous, never fabricate zero' policy documented at the top of the same file is not applied to these two fields.
expected: Every badge count in this provider follows the same 'null/failure means UNKNOWN, hold the previous value' contract the file documents for messages/announcements/tasks.
actual: setCoachhelm(alerts.success ? ... : 0) and setNotificationsUnread(unread.success ? ... : 0), both also 0 in their catch blocks, fabricate a confident zero on any transient failure.
proposed_fix: Change both setters to hold the previous value on failure/exception instead of writing 0, matching the pattern already used for messages/announcements/tasks/travel/calendarNotifications a few lines above.

user_consequence: A player who opens the Announcements page and reads every posted announcement still carries an unread-looking badge (feeding the combined Team count, A09-001) for up to 24 hours after publish, because reading the page never clears it. The badge's 'unread' semantics for non-acknowledgement-required announcements are pure time-decay, not read state.
mechanism: getPlayerNotificationCountsImpl counts a non-ack-required announcement as unread whenever `Date.now() - published_at < 24h`, with zero reference to lastSeenAt or any per-player read marker (player-notifications.ts:212-222). markAnnouncementsSeen (the only function that advances the state row this count could reference) is called from exactly one place in the whole app -- the login/unseen-announcements modal (NewAnnouncementsModalWrapper.tsx:49) -- never from the actual Announcements route (src/app/golf/(dashboard)/dashboard/announcements/page.tsx), which fetches and renders the list but never touches badges.refetch() or markAnnouncementsSeen.
expected: Visiting/reading the Announcements page clears the portion of the badge attributable to non-acknowledgement-required announcements the player has now seen, per the state/interaction truth table's 'Committed'/'read' semantics (Section 9.2).
actual: The count is entirely time-based for that class of announcement; the Announcements page performs no mark-seen or badge-refetch call at all.
proposed_fix: Call markAnnouncementsSeen (or an equivalent per-visit marker) from the Announcements route itself -- mirroring FairwayTravel.tsx's existing `markTravelSeen().then(() => badges.refetch())` on-mount pattern -- and have the badge count check lastSeenAt for non-ack-required announcements instead of (or in addition to) the 24h window.

user_consequence: A player mid round-entry (or any active task) who receives a push notification gets a native iOS banner + sound (system-presented while the app is open) AND an in-app toast for the exact same event, plus a haptic buzz -- two competing presentations and a haptic for one event, which is the precise double-notification failure the attention policy is meant to prevent, and a real interruption risk during active data entry.
mechanism: capacitor.config.ts sets PushNotifications.presentationOptions to ['badge','sound','alert'], which (per the Capacitor push-notifications plugin) tells iOS to present the system alert+sound even while the WebView is foregrounded. Independently, initPushListeners' 'pushNotificationReceived' handler (push-registration.ts) fires fwHaptic('light') and dispatches PUSH_RECEIVED_EVENT; CapacitorProvider.tsx's onReceived listener turns that into a fairwayToast(...) in-app banner. Nothing suppresses the native alert when the in-app toast is about to render the same content, and nothing suppresses the toast/haptic when the app is in the foreground and the system will already show its own alert.
expected: One event produces exactly one presentation (native banner when backgrounded, one in-app affordance when foregrounded) plus at most one haptic, per Section 9.4's 'A button, handler and success toast cannot independently vibrate for the same event' and the work order's explicit double-notification requirement.
actual: presentationOptions always includes 'alert'+'sound' (foreground included) while the app additionally renders its own toast+haptic for the identical received event -- two banners, one haptic, every foreground push.
proposed_fix: Either drop 'alert'/'sound' from presentationOptions when the app can detect it is foregrounded (Capacitor's plugin does not expose a runtime per-notification override, so this likely means moving to a foreground-only in-app presentation and only allowing the system to show 'alert' while backgrounded, which needs an app-state check before deciding whether to also show the in-app toast), or drop the in-app toast/haptic entirely for foreground pushes and rely solely on the system presentation. Requires an explicit product decision on which channel wins in the foreground case -- flagged as an open question below.

user_consequence: With HELM_CUSTOMER_EMAIL_ENABLED off (the recorded current owner default), a player whose coach creates a new qualifier or assigns them a development plan receives literally zero signal of it -- no email (suppressed by the gate), no push, no bell/More entry, and no badge increment anywhere in GolfNavBadgeCounts. The only way to discover either event is to manually browse to Qualifiers or My Development. Task assignment is partially covered (the pendingTasks badge does increment via the real golf_task_assignments row) but still produces no push/bell signal, only a silent count bump.
mechanism: notifyQualifierCreated (called from golf.ts:4220) and notifyDevPlanAssigned (called from development.ts:339) both route exclusively through sendEmailNotificationDirect, which is now suppressed by gateCustomerEmail (outbound-gate.ts) -- correctly, per the recorded owner decision. Neither call site independently inserts a row into the generic `notifications` table (the one the unified bell/dispatch.ts/task-reminders.ts pipeline reads) nor increments any field in GolfNavBadgeCounts, unlike task-reminders.ts, which writes its own `notifications` row in addition to its (also gated) email.
expected: An event whose sole always-on delivery channel (customer email) is administratively disabled should still leave a discoverable in-app trace (a notifications row and/or a badge), per the work order's 'distinguish notification submission/acceptance from delivery' requirement -- a suppressed external channel should not silently become a total blackout.
actual: qualifier_created and dev_plan_assigned have no in-app fallback at all while the email gate is off; task_assigned has only the pendingTasks count, no bell/push presentation.
proposed_fix: Have notifyQualifierCreated and notifyDevPlanAssigned (and, for full parity, notifyTaskAssigned) also insert a `notifications` table row (mirroring task-reminders.ts's own insert) independent of whether the email send itself is gated, so the bell/More surfaces always reflect these events regardless of the email kill switch's state.

user_consequence: A user taps a push notification, is deep-linked straight to the exact object it named, clearly sees it -- and the corresponding bell badge count does not go down. The notification stays 'unread' until the user separately opens the bell panel and taps (or long-presses mark-all-read on) the same item again, which most users will never do, so the badge overcounts indefinitely relative to what the user has actually seen.
mechanism: pushNotificationActionPerformed (push-registration.ts) only validates the URL (isSafeInternalPath) and dispatches PUSH_NAVIGATE_EVENT for CapacitorProvider.tsx to router.push -- it never calls markNotificationRead or any equivalent write. The ONLY code paths that mark a `notifications`/`golf_calendar_notifications` row read are the bell's own handleItemClick (NotificationBell.tsx) and its 'Mark all read' button. No destination route (calendar, tasks, etc.) independently marks the originating notification read either.
expected: Per the work order: 'Test notification tap on cold/warm start ... does it resolve the named object/version, or just a broad screen? Is the target marked read before the applicable visibility rule says it was seen?' -- a push tap that lands the user on the named object should mark that notification read.
actual: The push tap path never marks anything read; read state is exclusively a bell-UI-click side effect.
proposed_fix: The push payload already carries enough identity to resolve a target (`data.url`); extend it (or the notification id already present in the payload) so pushNotificationActionPerformed can call markNotificationRead(id, source) before/alongside the navigate dispatch, the same way NotificationBell.handleItemClick does.

user_consequence: The same physical unread count renders as a different number depending on which of two badges in the SAME component happens to show it -- e.g. 15 unread renders '15' on an individual bottom-nav tab but '9+' on the aggregate More column -- reproducing, inside one file, the exact rail-vs-bottom-nav cap mismatch a prior fix (cited in-code as 'audit 2026-07-24, M2') already corrected once.
mechanism: FairwayBottomNav.tsx renders a per-item badge with `item.badge > 99 ? '99+' : item.badge` (comment explicitly there to keep this cap matching the rail), but the same file's aggregate More badge caps at `moreBadge > 9 ? '9+' : moreBadge` about 55 lines later -- an independent, lower cap for the same underlying data shape.
expected: One display-cap convention per numeric badge across the whole shell (per the M2 fix's own stated intent).
actual: Two different caps (99+ vs 9+) coexist in the same component file.
proposed_fix: Use the same 99+ cap (or a single shared formatBadgeCount helper) for the aggregate More badge as the per-item badge already uses.

user_consequence: If the bell panel is reopened while the backend is degraded, a user with an already-populated list sees no indication anything is wrong -- the list simply stops updating with no 'stale' or 'retry' affordance, only a silently swallowed error.
mechanism: NotificationBell wires `error={items.length === 0 ? error : null}` into NotificationFeedPanel -- deliberately correct for a genuinely empty first-load error (does not falsely say 'nothing here'), but it also means a background reload failure with an already non-empty `items` array discards the error entirely rather than surfacing a stale/retry cue, contrary to Section 9.1's 'Background refresh failed: Last confirmed same-scope result plus stale/retry indication when material.'
expected: A background refresh failure with existing content shown should surface a minimal stale/retry cue per the truth table, not disappear silently.
actual: The `error` value is unconditionally discarded whenever `items.length > 0`.
proposed_fix: Surface a small non-blocking stale indicator (e.g. a subtle banner or 'last updated' note) when a background reload fails with existing items still shown, instead of fully suppressing the error.
